title: Analogy Quality — Simple, Relatable, Non-Distracting
description: For the analogies that BELONG (concept_intro slides only — placement is scored by the analogy_placement set): they must be simple, everyday, and relatable, and must clarify the concept without distracting. No elaborate, niche, or multi-part analogies that need their own explanation, and no domain reused across slides.
criterion: 1-2 sentences, everyday domain, maps cleanly and STRUCTURALLY to the concept, ends with an explicit tie-back naming the concept, introduces no new confusion; no analogy or analogy DOMAIN repeated across slides.

rubric.5: Simple, relatable, illuminating, one clean mapping.
rubric.3: Works but slightly stretched or a touch long.
rubric.1: Complex/niche/distracting, or needs its own explanation, or repeated.

input.analogy: Like registered post — you get a delivery receipt for every letter.
Like a Formula-1 team's tyre-degradation model balancing undercut strategy against a virtual safety car window while managing ERS deployment.

cases.rationale: Niche, complex, needs its own explanation — distracting.

input.note: identical postcard analogy already used on an earlier slide for IP

cases.rationale: Repeated analogy across slides — not allowed.

input.analogy: Like a long queue at a railway counter where everyone waits their turn — just as processes wait for resources.

cases.rationale: Structurally wrong: a queue is a linear wait, a deadlock cycle is circular. The tie-back is present but maps onto the wrong shape.
